finding: The design trajectory is borderline but does not reject its fitted stationary Gaussian AR1 error null at five percent. Both formerly held-out trajectories reject after AR persistence is estimated from linear-detrended residuals, one strongly. Residual lag-one and lag-two correlations remain modest. Correlated finite-population noise is present but does not fully explain the repeated held-out drift; the evidence supports a slow secular density-amplitude component superimposed on that noise.
limitations: Each AR1 error model is fitted to linear-detrended residuals from the same series being tested.
The Gaussian AR1 assumption is only a first-order approximation to the birth-loss process.
The previously held-out seeds became design evidence when this post-protocol analysis was performed and cannot be reused for future confirmation.
Failure to reject a stationary null is not proof of stationarity.
decision: Retain the completed protocol_not_confirmed decision. Use these three trajectories only for designing an uncertainty-aware rule and require entirely new stochastic seeds for confirmation.
next_experiment: Before a new confirmation campaign, prospectively separate equilibration duration from macro-particle-count scaling. Require any higher-population run to reduce innovation variance consistently with inverse particle count, while a longer-equilibration control must remove the secular component without shifting the mean Turner profile, current, or normalized shape.
claim_boundary: This exploratory result supports a real slow density-amplitude component in addition to correlated finite-population noise. It does not identify its physical cause, validate Turner Case 1, prove stationarity, or authorize profile pooling.
